title: Queensland Snake ID
subtitle: Venomous & harmless snakes and legless lizards
intro: Real photos from iNaturalist observers in Queensland. Decide whether it's dangerous, then name the species.
fieldRule: Field rule: in Australia, treat any snake you can't identify for certain as dangerous.

species.name: Oxyuranus scutellatus
species.note: Long, pale-faced head; uniform brown with a paler snout and orange-tinged eyes. Large, fast and nervous.

species.name: Oxyuranus microlepidotus
species.note: Dark glossy head (darker in winter); scales edged dark, giving a herringbone look. Channel Country of the far south-west.

species.name: Pseudonaja textilis
species.note: Slender, plain tan to dark brown; cream belly with orange or pink spots. Juveniles banded with a black head and nape.

species.name: Pseudonaja mengdeni
species.note: Very variable: plain, banded or black-headed. Dry inland country.

species.name: Pseudonaja aspidorhyncha
species.note: Squarish snout; inland plains and downs. Often dark on the head and neck.

species.name: Pseudonaja guttata
species.note: Yellow-brown to orange with dark-edged scales forming speckles. Black-soil plains.

species.name: Pseudonaja ingrami
species.note: Robust, glossy brown with a darker head. Cracking clays of the Barkly Tableland.

species.name: Pseudonaja nuchalis
species.note: Variable; often a dark nape band or herringbone pattern. Tropical woodland and Gulf country.

species.name: Acanthophis antarcticus
species.note: Thick body, broad triangular head, thin pale tail tip used as a lure. Banded grey, brown or red. Lies still in leaf litter.

species.name: Acanthophis praelongus
species.note: Rough-looking scales and raised ridges over the eyes. Tropical north.

species.name: Acanthophis rugosus
species.note: Stout and banded with rough, keeled scales. Barkly Tableland and the Gulf country of north-west Queensland.

species.name: Pseudechis australis
species.note: Large and heavy with a broad head. Each scale two-toned, giving a netted look. Absent from the far south-east.

species.name: Pseudechis porphyriacus
species.note: Glossy black back, red to pink lower flanks. Usually near water along the east coast.

species.name: Pseudechis guttatus
species.note: Black, grey or cream-spotted; blue-grey belly. Inland of the Great Dividing Range.

species.name: Pseudechis colletti
species.note: Dark with bold pink-orange to cream bands or blotches. Black-soil downs of central-west Queensland only.

species.name: Pseudechis papuanus
species.note: Plain black. Torres Strait islands near New Guinea.

species.name: Tropidechis carinatus
species.note: Strongly keeled scales; olive-brown with narrow dark crossbands. Easily mistaken for the harmless Keelback, but has no loreal scale.

species.name: Notechis scutatus
species.note: Yellowish crossbands on dark olive, or plain. Flattens its neck. Border ranges and Granite Belt.

species.name: Hoplocephalus stephensii
species.note: Dark and cream bands; barred lips. Climbs in rainforest and tall forest.

species.name: Hoplocephalus bitorquatus
species.note: Grey body; pale band behind the head edged with black. Climbs in woodland trees.

species.name: Cryptophis nigrescens
species.note: Glossy black, tiny eyes, pink to cream belly. Nocturnal in east-coast forest.

species.name: Pseudechis pailsei
species.note: A smaller relative of the Mulga Snake with the same netted, two-toned scales. Rocky country of the north-west.

species.name: Pseudonaja modesta
species.note: Small. Brown with a black head blotch and narrow dark rings that fade with age.

species.name: Denisonia devisi
species.note: Stout; yellow-brown with ragged dark bands; barred lips. Floodplains.

species.name: Denisonia maculata
species.note: Brown with dark-edged white lip bars. Gilgai wetlands of central Queensland; threatened.

species.name: Demansia psammophis
species.note: Slender, big eyes; pale-edged dark comma below the eye. Active by day and very fast.

species.name: Demansia papuensis
species.note: Large, dark grey to black, with a long thin tail. Tropical woodland.

species.name: Demansia vestigiata
species.note: Dark grey-brown with fine flecks; slender with big eyes.

species.name: Demansia torquata
species.note: Dark collar across the neck; pale-edged eye marking.

species.name: Hemiaspis signata
species.note: Olive to black with two thin pale lines on the face; dark belly. Near water.

species.name: Hemiaspis damelii
species.note: Grey above; young have a black head. Floodplain country; threatened.

species.name: Cryptophis boschmai
species.note: Brown with paler lips; small and nocturnal.

species.name: Cryptophis nigrostriatus
species.note: Pink-red to salmon with a black stripe down the back.

species.name: Suta suta
species.note: Dark hood on the head, pale-edged eye line. Coils tightly when threatened.

species.name: Suta dwyeri
species.note: Black cap on the head and nape; reddish-brown body. Nocturnal.

species.name: Cacophis squamulosus
species.note: Yellow stripe along each side of the head forming a crown; pink-orange belly with a dark midline.

species.name: Cacophis harriettae
species.note: Black with a bright white band around the back of the head.

species.name: Cacophis krefftii
species.note: Tiny; black with a yellow-cream band on the nape and a yellow belly.

species.name: Cacophis churchilli
species.note: Tiny; dark grey with a pale nape band. Wet Tropics.

species.name: Furina diadema
species.note: Dark-edged reddish scales; glossy black head with a red-orange nape patch.

species.name: Furina ornata
species.note: Like the Red-naped Snake but with an orange nape band. Northern and inland.

species.name: Furina barnardi
species.note: Yellow-brown with dark-edged scales and a pale nape band.

species.name: Furina dunmalli
species.note: Grey to black with pale lips. Brigalow belt; threatened.

species.name: Furina tristis
species.note: Dark brown with a pale nape band. Cape York.

species.name: Vermicella annulata
species.note: Bold black and white rings. Lifts its body in stiff loops when threatened.

species.name: Brachyurophis australis
species.note: Coral-pink to orange with narrow pale-edged bands; black bands on head and neck; upturned snout.

species.name: Antaioserpens albiceps
species.note: Reddish-brown with a darker head. Burrows; rarely seen.

species.name: Aipysurus laevis
species.note: Large, olive-brown above, cream below. Curious around divers on the Great Barrier Reef.

species.name: Aipysurus duboisii
species.note: Pinkish-olive with dark-edged scales. Reef flats.

species.name: Hydrophis platurus
species.note: Black back, yellow belly, spotted paddle tail. Open ocean; often washes up on beaches.

species.name: Hydrophis elegans
species.note: Long body with a small head; banded. Turbid inshore water.

species.name: Hydrophis major
species.note: Olive head with broad dark bands on the body.

species.name: Hydrophis stokesii
species.note: Very thick-bodied; variable bands.

species.name: Hydrophis peronii
species.note: Spiny projections above the eyes.

species.name: Hydrophis kingii
species.note: Dark head with pale markings like spectacles.

species.name: Hydrophis curtus
species.note: Short and stout with enlarged keeled belly scales.

species.name: Hydrophis ocellatus
species.note: Pale with dark bands or rings of spots. Reef and inshore waters.

species.name: Emydocephalus annulatus
species.note: Blunt, turtle-like head. Often banded black and cream; eats fish eggs.

species.name: Boiga irregularis
species.note: Big eyes with vertical pupils, bulbous head, thin neck; banded brown or red and cream. Nocturnal and quick to strike.

species.name: Cerberus australis
species.note: Eyes on top of the head. Mangrove mudflats.

species.name: Pseudoferania polylepis
species.note: Olive-brown with small upward-facing eyes. Freshwater.

species.name: Fordonia leucobalia
species.note: Very variable colour; white belly. Eats crabs in mangroves.

species.name: Myron richardsonii
species.note: Small and grey-banded. Mangroves.

species.name: Tropidonophis mairii
species.note: Keeled scales like the dangerous Rough-scaled Snake, but has a loreal scale between eye and nostril. Olive-brown with dark flecks; near water; eats cane toads.

species.name: Dendrelaphis punctulatus
species.note: Very slender with huge eyes; green, olive, black or blue above with a yellow throat. Shows blue skin when it inflates its neck.

species.name: Dendrelaphis calligaster
species.note: Slender and brown above with a dark stripe through the eye; pale belly.

species.name: Stegonotus australis
species.note: Glossy slate-grey with a white belly. Bites readily but is harmless.

species.name: Acrochordus granulatus
species.note: Loose, granular skin; banded. Estuaries and coastal water.

species.name: Acrochordus arafurae
species.note: Baggy, rough skin. Freshwater billabongs and rivers.

species.name: Morelia spilota
species.note: Heat-sensing pits along the lips; blotched or banded pattern. Large; common in roofs and sheds.

species.name: Morelia viridis
species.note: Adults bright green; young yellow or red. Coils over a branch. Iron and McIlwraith Ranges.

species.name: Simalia kinghorni
species.note: Australia's longest snake; iridescent with zigzag patterns and large head scales.

species.name: Liasis fuscus
species.note: Iridescent dark brown to black above, yellow below. Near water.

species.name: Liasis olivaceus
species.note: Large, plain olive-brown. Rocky country of the north-west.

species.name: Aspidites melanocephalus
species.note: Glossy black head and neck; banded body; no heat pits.

species.name: Aspidites ramsayi
species.note: Banded orange-brown with dark patches above the eyes. Sandy inland country.

species.name: Antaresia maculosa
species.note: Small python with dark irregular blotches on a pale ground. Rocky outcrops and caves.

species.name: Antaresia childreni
species.note: Small and brown with faded blotches.

species.name: Antaresia stimsoni
species.note: Small, with bold reddish blotches on cream.

species.name: Anilios ligatus
species.note: Worm-like; tiny eye spots, blunt head and a spine-tipped tail.

species.name: Anilios nigrescens
species.note: Worm-like; dark purplish-grey above, pink below.

species.name: Anilios wiedii
species.note: Small and slender with a brownish snout.

species.name: Indotyphlops braminus
species.note: Tiny, shiny dark worm-like snake. Introduced; often in pot plants.

species.name: Anilios torresianus
species.note: Worm-like with tiny eye spots and a spine-tipped tail. Wet Tropics and Cape York.

species.name: Lialis burtonis
species.note: A lizard: long wedge-shaped snout, ear opening, tiny hindlimb flaps and a fleshy tongue. Colour is extremely variable.

species.name: Pygopus lepidopodus
species.note: A lizard: ear opening, hindlimb flaps, broad fleshy tongue; rows of dark spots.

species.name: Pygopus schraderi
species.note: A lizard with dark head and nape bands that mimic a young brown snake.

species.name: Paradelma orientalis
species.note: A grey lizard with a pale nape band. Brigalow belt; threatened.

species.name: Delma tincta
species.note: A slender lizard with dark bars on the head. Leaps and flicks wildly when disturbed.

species.name: Delma torquata
species.note: A small lizard with dark bands on the head and neck. Threatened.

species.name: Delma plebeia
species.note: A plain grey-brown lizard with pale lips.

species.name: Pygopus steelescotti
species.note: A lizard with a dark hood on the head and neck, like a young brown snake. Ear opening and hindlimb flaps give it away.

species.name: Delma inornata
species.note: A plain olive-brown lizard with pale lips. Grassland and open woodland.
